messages:
pat: hitting a nasty onboarding loop behind our corporate proxy. `redwoodctl login` opens the browser, I authenticate, but the CLI reports: `error: tls: certificate signed by unknown authority` when it tries to fetch the token from the callback URL.
yun: are you on mac/linux? do you have HTTPS_PROXY or HTTP_PROXY set? corp proxies often MITM TLS with a private root.
pat: macOS, yes we set HTTPS_PROXY to http://proxy.corp:8080. curl to public sites works after installing corp root in Keychain. But `redwoodctl login` (browser flow) fails on the callback fetch:
```
2026-03-10T09:15:02Z info opening browser for auth
2026-03-10T09:15:25Z error callback fetch failed: Get "https://127.0.0.1:51112/callback?code=...": x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
```
pat: weirdly `redwoodctl login --device` works (I get the device code and can complete login), token is written to ~/.config/redwood/token, but when I run `redwoodctl local-serve` next it errors trying to refresh the token with the same x509 error.
aoife: likely the CLI's HTTP client uses a CA bundle that doesn't include your corp root. On mac we try system roots, but boxed builds (our static binaries) include a bundled cert pool which ignores Keychain updates.
yun: repro suggestion: run `REDWOOD_DEBUG_HTTP=1 redwoodctl login` and capture TLS handshake. If it's using a bundled bundle you'll see the client certpool path in logs.
pat: debug shows `tls: client using embedded cert pool` and `GET https://auth.redwood.ai/token -> x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`. So yeah embedded CA bundle causing issue.
aoife: options: 1) tell users to run with `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`/`SSL_CERT_FILE` env var pointing at PEM that includes corp root; 2) detect HTTPS_PROXY + test connection to auth host and fall back to device flow automatically; 3) add CLI flag `--skip-cert-verify` for dev but with huge warning; 4) ship a small helper `redwoodctl trust-cert /path/to/corp.pem` that merges into our cert pool for the installed binary.
yun: we should avoid recommending `--insecure` in docs. Better UX: if the CLI detects TLS chain validation failure and env HTTPS_PROXY is present, prompt: "We detected a corporate proxy intercepting TLS. Would you like to (a) use device flow (recommended), (b) point redwoodctl at a CA bundle, or (c) run with --insecure for this session?"
aoife: also add `redwoodctl doctor --certs` which tries to curl the auth endpoint and prints whether system and bundled CA pools accept the server cert and gives remediation steps. That would cut support churn.
pat: small workaround that worked for me: `curl --cacert /path/to/corp-root.pem https://auth.redwood.ai/.well-known/openid-configuration` verified CA works; then `export SSL_CERT_FILE=/path/to/merged-ca.pem` and `redwoodctl login` browser flow succeeded. But onboarding doc should include this.
yun: backend note: refresh token calls come from workers and from local CLI; ensure both use the same cert handling code path. If one uses system libs and another uses bundled code we'll create intermittent failures.
aoife: filing issue with repro steps and suggested UX changes. Also add e2e test matrix where HTTPS_PROXY is set and custom CA is injected to ensure device-flow fallback works.
dev-bot: created issue DX-1701: "CLI browser login fails behind corporate HTTPS proxy (x509: certificate signed by unknown authority); add device-flow fallback, doctor checks, and trust-cert helper" assigned to @aoife P2.
pat: thanks, will paste logs and the merged CA file path in the issue. :thumbsup:
